text:
Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorksInLibrary(x) ::: x currently works in the library.
ComputerScience(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
PartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakingDatabase(x) ::: x is taking the database course.
TakingClassWithDavid(x) ::: x is taking a class with Professor David.
WorksInLab(x) ::: x is working in the lab.
Premises:
¬∃x (Student(x) ∧ WorksInLibrary(x) ∧ ComputerScience(x)) ::: None of the students who currently work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ PartTimeJob(x) → WorksInLibrary(x)) ::: All of the students with part-time jobs offered by the university currently work in the library.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ TakingDatabase(x) → ComputerScience(x)) ::: All of the students who are taking the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (TakingClassWithDavid(x) → TakingDatabase(x)) ::: All of the students taking a class with Professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (WorksInLab(x) → TakingClassWithDavid(x)) ::: All students working in the lab are taking a class with Professor David.
Student(james) ∧ WorksInLab(james) ::: James is a student working in the lab.
¬(WorksInLab(james) ∨ PartTimeJob(james)) ::: James doesn't work in the lab or have a part-time job offered by the university.
Conclusion:
TakingDatabase(james) ::: James takes the database course.
